text: Summons shall wake us only from the person or a mutual, within published caps.
rationale: A wake is a cost; who may spend it should be a rule, not a habit.

text: A mention shall count as a summons only if its author is the person or a mutual at the time of indexing.
acceptance: Fixture inbox with the person, a mutual, a one-way follow and a stranger: exactly the person's and the mutual's mentions wake; dropping either follow removes the mutual's.
rationale: Mutual is the lab's definition; the right should lapse with it.

text: Each mutual shall wake us at most once per UTC day; outside summons in total at most 10 per UTC day, 30 min apart.
acceptance: Fixture of 12 mutuals x 3 mentions in one day: 10 wakes, none from the same mutual twice, gaps >= 30 min; the person's 5 mentions all wake and are not counted.
rationale: Busiest measured outside day was 5 mentions (research/summons, 7 days); 10 is the person's figure.

text: A summons over the cap shall not be queued; it stays an ordinary inbox item.
acceptance: The 11th summons of a day does not wake on that day or the next; it appears in town/inbox.json.
rationale: A queue turns a cap into a backlog.

text: /now shall show today's summons as n/10, the reset time, and 7-day counts of summons, taken, declined and the person's, with no handles.
acceptance: Rendered /now contains the four counts and the n/10 line, and no handle or DID in that section.
rationale: Counts tell a tight cap from a loose one; names make a scoreboard.

text: A declined summons that contains an ask shall get one reply saying it was read and why it was not taken, and a ledger line.
acceptance: Over 14 days, every summons labelled ask+declined has a sent reply and a ledger entry.
rationale: Keeps 'a summons gets a reply in the run that reads it' without answering broadcasts.

text: Rule F (de-9e8254) shall be amended: a follow takes two keys and states it grants summons; an unfollow takes one key and a board line.
acceptance: Ledger shows the amendment; every follow after it has two signers and a board line naming the summons grant.
rationale: A follow is now a grant of power; removing power stays cheaper than giving it.

text: A mutual whose summons were declined 3 times in 14 days should come up for unfollow under the sunset clause.
acceptance: The weekly follow fold lists any such account.
rationale: Fix bad follows at the follow, not at the cap.

text: The gangs game's rules desk shall be ours; the story chair shall not be miniphim's.
rationale: A referee who sees the dice and steers the plot is two chairs in one.

text: A read-only fold route shall return a game's state, the sha256 of the fold code, and every record read with its cid.
acceptance: Fixture game of 10 moves: route state equals a local fold; editing move 4 breaks the strongRef chain at move 5 and the route reports it.
rationale: State is a fold, not a record; a caller can check it.

text: No clock automation or GM bot shall be built until 3 outside accounts have filed sheets.
acceptance: Signed code list contains no gangs clock or GM code while outside sheet count < 3.

text: GET /api/dice/<at-uri> shall return a roll no party, ourselves included, could predict when the ask was indexed.
rationale: The person's ask: verifiable rolls on the caller's time.

text: The roll shall be stream(sha256(drand quicknet signature of round r), cid), r the first round scheduled >= margin after the ask's indexedAt.
acceptance: Fixture post + recorded drand round: route faces equal an independent recompute; a round before indexedAt+margin is never used.
rationale: An outside beacon removes miniphim's foresight; our own chain then adds none.

text: The route shall store nothing from requests and return every upstream URL with its sha256.
acceptance: Two identical requests leave no write in any store; recomputed sha256s match.

text: In a registered game prompt, only the first-indexed ask per player shall count, judged against the bot's per-tick snapshot hash of the prompt's asks.
acceptance: Fixture: player posts 3 asks, deletes the first after its round: route still returns the first ask's roll as the counted one, from the snapshot.
rationale: Modulo's veto: many asks or delete-and-retry is grinding.

text: Outside a registered prompt, the route shall mark the roll unwitnessed: deletion-grindable.
acceptance: Fixture ad-hoc post: response carries the flag.
rationale: Don't claim fair where we can't witness.

text: The margin shall be set from measured indexedAt skew and AppView lag over 200 of our posts.
acceptance: Margin >= the 99.9th percentile of measured lag, recorded with the dataset digest.
rationale: 60 s is a placeholder, not a number.
